keyPhrases.text: tedious play that's stubbornly unaffecting, its pathos hollow and manufactured
Daniel Sullivan's Broadway production has elegance to spare
a lot of care and effort has been put into a play that acquires a pulse only intermittently

reasoning: The review opens with harsh criticism calling the play 'tedious,' 'stubbornly unaffecting' with 'hollow and manufactured' pathos. While it praises production values and some performances (Clark, Burstein), the fundamental assessment is negative - describing a play that 'acquires a pulse only intermittently' despite technical excellence. The critique outweighs the praise, placing this in negative territory but not a complete pan due to acknowledged merits in design and select performances.
